attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own published post, offered in his own voice.

semantics.note: Faithful enough. It keeps the 'almost always' quantifier, the crypto analogy and the $15B premise. The $15B appears inside a rhetorical question but is presented as fact, so treating it as a premise is reasonable.

contract.note: The plain reading of 'almost always' as 'nearly all, not just a majority' is ordinary and fair. Tying $15B to the linked PitchBook figure for H1 2023 generative AI matches the speaker's own source. The August 2023 window was chosen by the evaluator but is reasonable.

evidence.note: CNN/PitchBook: $15.2B into generative AI globally in H1 2023. This matches the contract's funding scope and confirms the rounded $15B figure. It says nothing about how often discussion was future-focused.

Tow Center (May 2023) describes both speculative coverage and steady reporting on what companies were actually doing. It is from an earlier period and has no frequency measure, so it cannot settle 'almost always'.

Peer-reviewed study of UK headlines from Jan–May 2023: coverage was sensationalised, swinging between promise and danger. It is UK-only, from an earlier period, and does not code future vs present, so it is not a matched measure.

reviews.rationale: The funding premise holds: PitchBook via CNN reports about $15.2B for H1 2023. The core claim does not resolve. The packet has no representative analysis of August 2023 AI discussion that separates future possibilities from existing developments, and none for the crypto analogy. e2 and e3 come from earlier periods and do not measure that split, so 'almost always' is neither shown nor refuted.
